framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisitions and material changes in shareholding; prescribes filing deadlines and content requirements for acquirers crossing statutory thresholds.
Defines threshold events (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 75%, 90%) and exemptions (creeping acquisitions up to 5% per financial year; employee share schemes; inter-se transfers; inheritance).
Sets out open offer obligations when acquiring 25% or more; exemptions available for certain classes of acquirers and transactions.
Defines control and change of control; material for assessing whether the acquisition triggers mandatory open offer or exemption application.
Material event and Associated Party Transactions disclosure requirements for listed companies; impacts Britannia's announcement obligations on receipt of substantial acquisition notice.

headline: Associated Biscuits International Discloses Substantial Acquisition in Britannia Industries under SEBI SAST Regulations
sum: Associated Biscuits International has filed a regulatory disclosure under SEBI Regulation 31(4) of the Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, 2011, indicating a material shareholding event in Britannia Industries Limited. The filing marks a significant transparency requirement for substantial acquisitions in a major FMCG listed company.
detail: Associated Biscuits International Limited has submitted a Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE regarding a substantial acquisition event in Britannia Industries Limited, a flagship FMCG company listed on both BSE and NSE. Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI SAST Regulations mandates disclosure of changes in shareholding that cross prescribed thresholds or material movements in existing substantial holdings. The filing represents a key transparency mechanism under takeover law and may trigger additional compliance obligations (open offer, exemption orders, or competing bids) depending on the acquirer's intent, acquisition percentage, and control implications.
